page.layout: One column of running text, with a centred chapter heading, a centred italic title and a woodcut initial. Above the text, the running head with the page number. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: speramus, ad omnium convictionem. Dein relinquit nos
hic locus adhuc de anni tempestate incertos, cujus
quaestionis discussio longe aliud quoque requirit funda-
mentum, in sequentibus revelandum. Ut proin hic
locus ad quaestionem nostram quidem multum lucis af-
ferat, sed solus omnem caussam non absolvat. Scripsit
quidem Magnus ille Scaliger de emendat. temporum
libr. 6. Unus tantum locus in evangelio relictus est, cujus

l.i: auxilio aetatem Christi & ejus natalis annum

main_text.l: colligere datum est: quem ajit in Luca cap. 3 : 1. 33. in-
veniri. Veruntamen, nisi alius esset, qui rem strictius
definiat, & quasdam in isto testimonio latitudines
certiori calculo restringat, fatendum foret eum locum solum
quaestioni decidendae haud parem fore.
CAPUT V.

l.i: Calculo ephemeriarum solo etiam nati Christi mensem

main_text.l: Q[?]uoniam circa diem Christo natalem adeo
inconstans est veterum traditio, dum
alii eum vigente brumâ (sive 25 December,
sive 6 Ianuarii) alii vernali tempestate (sive
25 Pachon sive Pharmuthi) alii tandem
sub autumno natum voluerint: primus omnium fuit
illustris Scaliger, qui in invento anno Christi natali nobis
spem fecit adinveniendi quoque ejusdem tempesta-
tem, atque mensem, & praeter propter diem, nati
Christi memoriae consonum. Viri acutissimi consilium
erat,

page.notes: The woodcut initial is a decorated letter; I read it as Q and marked it [?]. The old figure for 5 in "25" is printed like a long s; I read it as 25 in both places. The reference "3 : 1. 33." is set small and italic and is hard to read; I copied it as it appears. The words "af-ferat", "in-veniri" and "tempesta-tem" are split at line ends, and the printed hyphens are kept. The page has no marginal notes, and the margins hold only ornaments and specks, which I left out.
